questions.key_step: Bound S by a rectangle, a concave-chord trapezium and step rectangles; judge four inequalities.
questions.justification: Four statements each needing a different bounding idea (monotone comparison, concavity, step rectangles); no integration possible, so each needs a genuine check. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q3 (L4) but only bounds, so one lower.

questions.key_step: Split at pi/4 where |cos-sin| changes form; gap is 2 sin x / 2 cos x.
questions.justification: Routine split-and-integrate of two trigonometric curves with a modulus; options to check against.

questions.key_step: e^{-2x}f(x) is decreasing, so f<e^{2x-1}; integrate.
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (integrating factor for a differential inequality, then integral bound); idea is familiar but the inequality route is not routine.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the area identity once more: f(a)=F''(a).
questions.justification: Leibniz rule with variable limits twice, with a numerical answer; unfamiliar to see 'area = F'(a)+2' as an identity in a. Slightly harder than a plain chain.

questions.key_step: Four unrelated short items: sine-rule identity, quadratic in ratio, point-line distance, area with modulus.
questions.justification: Four items from three chapters, each short; the (D) area with a modulus and the (A) identity need care. Matching format allows elimination but several items must all be right.

questions.key_step: Shift origin to (-3,0); trapezium minus two curve-areas.

questions.key_step: Equate the area to the left of x=alpha to 1/8; quartic in alpha.
questions.justification: Direct bisection of an area leads to a biquadratic; checking four options is routine.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the integral equation to the linear ODE f'-2f=2x-3; then area.
questions.justification: Integral equation to linear DE to solution, then an area between a circle and a line; two chapters, four statements.

questions.key_step: Area between y=x and y=x^n is 1/2-1/(n+1).

questions.key_step: For x<1 f=0; the curves meet where e^{2(x-1)}=3.
questions.justification: Piecewise exponentials with a modulus, intersection via e^{2t}=3 and two integrals; more exact computation than a routine area question.
